participationLead: Not doing the whole ride? You can still come.

items.question: Where do we start, and when will you announce it?
Can I join partway through?
items.answerHtml: Yes. Meet the group at any brewery stop. Many riders join at the first brewery. We’ll announce its location and meetup time when confirmed.

items.question: Can I come if I don't ride a bicycle?
items.answerHtml:
Absolutely. Check the schedule and meet your friends at a brewery. You can join the roomful of Santas without riding between stops.

Or invite some unsuspecting friends out for lunch at one of our stops. Plan to arrive about 30 minutes before we do.

Don’t tell them about the Santas. Let us be the surprise.

items.question: Do I need to register?
items.answerHtml: No. The ride is free and there is no registration. Show up and ride. You can RSVP on Facebook, it’s optional, but appreciated!

items.question: Can I come alone?
items.answerHtml: Yes. You don’t need to know anyone to join us. Come on your own or bring a friend. Put on your Santa suit, say hello, and ride with the group.

items.question: Do I have to dress like Santa?
items.answerHtml: A Santa suit is the idea, and most of us wear one. You’re still welcome if you turn up as something else. We’ve had Christmas trees, Krampus, and a whole assortment of characters from the old stop-motion Christmas specials.

items.question: What if there's snow?
items.answerHtml:
We’ve ridden through snowstorms, ice, freezing rain and, unfortunately, increasingly warm weather. Christmas is starting to feel like Christmas in July. Yikes.

It’s Minneapolis in December, so dress appropriately. We’re seeing more and more fat bikes on the ride these days. They’ve become pretty common. If there’s snow or ice, studded tires are recommended.

Ultimately, ride only in conditions you’re comfortable with, and make sure your bike is set up accordingly. Even in the coldest years, people often start shedding layers by midday.

You may see Santas ducking into brewery bathrooms to peel off sweaty sweatpants beneath their costumes.

Turns out Santa suits don’t breathe particularly well.

items.question: Are kids allowed?
items.answerHtml:
Sorta. Kids need to be with a parent or guardian, but this isn’t an event made for kids. We pride ourselves on not being rowdy, but it’s still a winter brewery ride with adults drinking. The full ride is about 15 miles, conditions can be icy, and the last stops are after dark.

If you bring kids, use your judgment about the conditions and distance. Joining for one or two stops earlier in the day may be a better fit than the full ride. If you’re driving between stops, stay sober.

Ride at your own risk and follow traffic laws.

items.question: Do I have to drink?
items.answerHtml:
Nope. Drinking is entirely optional. You're here to ride bikes, wear festive costumes, and spread some holiday cheer.

If you do get smashed, lock up your bike and call a Lyft. Seriously.

One infamous year, we had half a dozen college students who were completely trashed by the second stop, riding down the middle of the road in a blizzard.

We'd prefer not to repeat that particular Christmas miracle.

items.question: Can I bring a toy to donate?
items.answerHtml: Yes. Bring a new, unwrapped toy. Gifts are for kids in need. Carry yours on your bike, like Santa carrying presents in his sleigh.

items.question: Is this a race?
items.answerHtml: Absolutely not. It's a social group ride.
